![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

There is an inconsistency between the card component's background color defined here ("#FFFFFF") and the description of the "Surface" color on line 102, which states that the "Surface (#100f1c)" color is used for "card backgrounds". To maintain design system consistency and honor the dark aesthetic, the card background color should be updated to use the surface color token.

```suggestion
  card:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.surface}"
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

This prose description of the card component specifies a "White background", which contradicts the "Surface" color description on line 102 ("Deep near-black for card backgrounds"). It should be updated to specify the dark surface background to align with the late-night glam aesthetic.

```suggestion
### Cards
- Dark surface background (`{colors.surface}`), 24px padding, 12px rounded corners, subtle shadow (0 2px 8px).
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep fault fixtures typed as unknown**

When `createMockPromptCompilerSeam('fault')` uses this helper, the intentionally invalid `compiledPromptFaultFixture` is cast back to `CompiledPrompt`, so any type-safe caller of the mock can now receive empty prompts as a valid contract output. This reintroduces the same type-safety leak the change is trying to remove; keep the fault branch as `unknown` and only pass it directly to `validateCompiledPrompt()` in the negative test.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor the compiler input in the mock**

When a test uses this mock with any valid input other than `promptCompilerInputFixture` (for example a different description or `addCaption: false`), `compile()` still returns the baked kitten prompt and `Glam Kitty` metadata. That no longer models the `compile(input)` seam and can let downstream tests pass while the request and compiled prompt disagree; either derive the fixture from the input scenario or reject inputs that do not match the selected fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the Cipher Gate for seam edits**

Because this commit changes `PromptCompilerSeam`/`GalleryStoreSeam`, the repo’s `AGENTS.md` requires a `DECISIONS.md` Cipher Gate entry with the touched seams and evidence paths. I checked `DECISIONS.md`, and the latest Cipher Gate entries are still dated 2026-05-16, so these 2026-05-28 seam changes have no evidence-linked summary for `npm run cipher:gate`/audit review even though the commit adds `docs/evidence/2026-05-28/*`; add the missing 2026-05-28 entry pointing at the new evidence outputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return a fresh compiled prompt per mock call**

When any test or caller mutates the object returned by `compile()` (for example trimming `metadata.enforcedConstraints` or editing `imagePrompt` while exercising downstream code), this now mutates the imported `compiledPromptFixture` itself, so later mock calls and fixture-based assertions in the same Vitest process can become order-dependent. The previous implementation created a new `CompiledPrompt` object for each call; keep that isolation by returning a deep clone or frozen copy of the fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
